excerpt: Headless 3D and VFX engine for agents. Research preview. - voyager-so/vork
content_html:
vork is a 3D and VFX engine built for AI agents.

Agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens.

skim-hero.mp4

One million birds, each on its own path. 192 frames at 1080p rendered in 97 seconds on a single NVIDIA L4. Blender EEVEE at the same sample count is projected at 13–18 minutes. How we measured · how it's made · credits

  • Built for agents: a small API that agents can extend with their own GPU programs.
  • Fast: 1.1–2.3× faster than EEVEE on default stills and movies, and about 8–11× on the bird flock. Speed, with the qualifications.
  • Native GPU engine: written in Rust and Slang, runs on Vulkan and Metal (Linux, Windows, macOS).

Paste this to your agent

Install vork, then paste:

Run vork init my-shot, read vork help, render a preview and inspect the image. Refine the camera and lighting before rendering at final quality. Read the relevant help topic when you need a feature the first page doesn't explain.

vork is written in Rust and Slang, with GPU rendering through Vulkan and Metal. An agent writes a scene, renders it, looks at the result and revises the code. There is no editor to drive.

Most creative tools expose controls that a person can operate. An agent can also write a shader in the middle of a shot. vork gives it geometry, ray queries and GPU execution, then lets scene programs define materials, cameras, light propagation, simulation and compositing. Ordinary shots need only scene data; the programming hooks are there when the shot needs something unusual.

Source-available and free during the research preview.

Start here

After installing vork, create a working project:

vork init my-shot
cd my-shot
vork render scene.json --out render.png
vork help

Open render.png, change a colour or camera position in scene.json, and render again. The starter uses only bundled sphere, box and grid primitives: no downloads, no GPU needed to initialize. Use vork init my-shot --language typescript or --language python for editable scene.ts or scene.py alongside the ready-to-render JSON. The generated README explains regeneration and SDK requirements. Existing files are never overwritten. The default std/final profile is warmed by setup; use --profile std/draft for quicker previews.

What you can make

The examples include code, preparation commands and credits. Large downloaded assets and footage stay outside Git; the recipes fetch them or accept a local path. The images here are stills from these shots. Keep each credit with its image.

Million birds

A million simulated agents steered by Slang compute programs, with a camera skimming through the flock. The camera and nine foreground birds are authored; the simulated million do not flap. The bird stills above come from the measured four-sample, denoised skim and reveal movies.

Credit: based on "Crow" by Alexei Ostapenko, CC BY 4.0. Changes: sampled flight pose, reduced distant mesh, rescaled, articulated flight wings, extracted wings for the starling body, resized textures. All bird and environment credits.

Cyber car

Watch the film: a car drives into the night as the forest turns into glowing cyan wireframe, drawn from real triangle edges by a scene shader.

Credit: “Car Concept” by Unity Fan, glTF adaptation by Eric Chadwick / Darmstadt Graphics Group, CC BY 4.0. Changes: scaled, animated, brighter head and tail lights, wheel pose. Trees, ground and asphalt from Poly Haven (CC0). The far mountains and sky are an image-model painting on a curved 3D card; everything else that moves is rendered.

VFX on real footage

Original footage Tracked camera and proxy geometry Final look

A procedural ceramic-and-bronze seed, a tracked camera, occlusion mattes and proxy geometry for relighting. The example teaches the base composite; the final look adds later relighting and wipes. Real footage + rendered 3D; no generative video.

Credit: footage by Ron Lach / Pexels, modified under the Pexels Licence. Original performer; no endorsement implied. Source and preparation.

After Rain

A suspended neon seed and blade sign added to a moving shot of an empty alley at night, with spill on the wall and reflections in the wet street. Real footage + rendered 3D; no generative video.

Credit: footage is "Ally" by Rafael Fernanz / Pexels, modified under the Pexels Licence. Source and preparation.

Black hole

The scene supplies a Schwarzschild light-propagation program through vork's public hook. Curved paths, capture and the disk's appearance live in the example. It is a numerical approximation, not an exact relativistic solver.

Credit: based on "Corinth Cargo Transporter" by Yvo Pors, CC BY 4.0. Changes: decimated geometry, resized, compressed and exposure-adjusted textures, adjusted material roughness and metallic weight, placement and scale. Ship credit.

Cake

A moving camera, depth of field and daylight on detailed scanned assets. This shot is rendered 3D, using Poly Haven assets; it isn't a photographed take.

Credit: Poly Haven CC0 assets; carrot cake photography by Greg Zaal, processing by James Ray Cock. Full cake credits.

Cozy Kitchen

Nicole Morena's Blender 3.5 splash scene, imported into vork. The recipe uses a shared material adaptation and a camera orbit; the pictured render has additional staging and animated lighting.

Credit: Cozy Kitchen by Nicole Morena, source .blend, CC BY-SA (version unspecified by source). Adapted and rendered in vork: camera orbit, animated lighting, widescreen framing, material translation and staging changes. This still and the adapted animation are shared under CC BY-SA. No artist endorsement implied. Changes and share-alike notice.

Water

A GPU liquid simulation implemented as Slang compute programs in vork's fluid library. It uses published APIC/FLIP and surface-reconstruction methods, with an authored initial impulse and limited secondary spray.

No suitable GPU?

Rendering requires Apple Silicon or an NVIDIA GPU with Vulkan ray queries. Scene authoring and vork help work without a GPU. On your own NVIDIA Linux machine, you can use the Docker runtime.

Give it to an agent

Start with vork init, then vork help. Scene JSON uses the stable editor schema. Use vork help for the starting scene and concepts, vork help TOPIC --all for topic fields, and vork help field PATH for an exact field reference.

Use the prompt above to start.

Python and TypeScript can author ordinary scene JSON through the SDKs. You can also write JSON directly. For example, save this as scene.json (also available as examples/first-scene.json):

{"version":2,"nodes":[
  {"type":"mesh","geometry":{"std":"sphere","radius":1},
   "materials":[{"inputs":{"base_color":[0.12,0.35,0.65],"specular_roughness":0.3}}]},
  {"type":"mesh","translation":[0,-1,0],"geometry":{"std":"grid","size":[10,10]},
   "materials":[{"inputs":{"base_color":[0.35,0.35,0.35]}}]},
  {"type":"light","shape":"rectangle","translation":[-3,5,4],"target":[0,0,0],
   "energy":700,"size":4,"color":[1,0.92,0.8]},
  {"type":"camera","translation":[3,2,5],"target":[0,0,0]}
],"render":{"resolution":[640,480]}}
vork render scene.json --profile std/previs --out preview.png
vork render scene.json --profile std/final --out final.png
vork help sdk
vork help programs --all

Scene content and render quality are separate. Use std/previs to iterate, std/draft for scene-ray lighting at 4 samples, std/final for the default delivery profile, and std/path for path transport. Final approximates indirect lighting and can darken interiors, including glossy bounces. More samples do not restore omitted transport; try path and inspect. Draft and final use 4 and 8 samples with bundled OIDN denoising by default; use --set denoise=false to turn it off. --set samples=N overrides the profile budget (1..4096); more samples means cleaner and slower. Without a fast GPU denoiser (NVIDIA or Apple GPU), draft and final say so and use 16 and 32 samples undenoised; --set denoise=true runs the slow CPU denoiser anyway. For a particular field, ask vork help field node.target. Help topics include exact fields with --all. Images, video and control passes come from the same scene; see vork help outputs.

Under the hood

Default rendering combines raster visibility with hardware ray-traced lighting; a path tracer is also available. The scene and render plan stay installed. Frames use retained GPU resources, with GPU-to-hardware-video encoding on supported native paths. A portable encoding fallback reads pixels back to the CPU.

Slang programs run on the GPU. Host parsing, planning, animation-track evaluation and IO still use the CPU. The public program hooks let a scene author change camera rays, material response, light propagation and film response without editing the renderer. vork help programs --all describes their scope.

Validation includes furnace tests and analytic oracles, alongside render tests. That is a way to catch errors, not a guarantee that every scene is physically exact.

Speed, with the qualifications

These are timings, not equal-quality speedups. The draft/final results come from the build identified by SHA-256 in the results report on an NVIDIA L4: final uses eight samples and OIDN, draft four and OIDN. All 152 planned jobs were accounted for. The broader sweep delivered 583 of 585 images; the million-stars stress scene ran out of GPU memory in both profiles. Visual review found softer edges, grainier defocus, wall mottling and changed sparse or spectral highlights at these budgets. Nineteen earlier quality comparisons failed their declared no-worse FLIP condition; that experiment was not repeated for this build.

vork times below are complete command wall times, including startup, scene loading, output writes and encoding. Setup, shader warmup, provisioning and transfers are excluded. Stills use five warm repetitions, movies three. Driver caches and clocks were not controlled. Blender 5.2.1 times are retained measured baselines, not fresh runs: EEVEE uses different settings, and its movie times exclude startup/loading after a still prime. Both movie timings include encoding. The car is a proxy. Benchmark method and recorded results explain the boundaries and carried-forward numbers.

Rerun

python3 benchmarks/fetch.py
python3 benchmarks/run.py --vork vork --out /tmp/vork-benchmark
python3 integrations/blender/benchmark.py --blender blender --out /tmp/blender-benchmark

The vork runner measures undenoised B-scene variants, not the denoised final8 tables above. It omits draft and does not set the recorded seed 11. The bird runner uses previs/final with a full-resolution warmup, not the recorded draft4 workflow. The final8/draft4 tables use build 81ae2b075; preview and path results come from earlier freezes, as noted beside those tables.

The Blender helper has been checked for preparation of all ten scenes on Blender 5.2.1. The historical GPU timing comparisons have not been rerun with this repair; see the method.

Research-preview limits

Participating media (fog, haze, smoke and volumes) are unsupported in 0.3. Used medium bindings and volume topology are refused; removed programs such as std/fog fail lookup even in unused definitions. Bake an image plate and composite it, or render the medium externally. For a deliberately dry alternative, remove medium-only nodes, bindings and definitions while preserving shared surfaces. See vork help upgrade and vork help limits.

Large scenes and dense transparency can fail, including on Mac; reducing image resolution alone does not necessarily fix them. Some heavy interiors work with std/path when the default hybrid profile fails. First use of a new program can involve substantial compilation, even after vork setup.

At four/eight samples, fine facades and hair can lose detail, defocus can show stepped or grainy edges, and sparse sparks or spectral highlights can change brightness and colour. Try --set samples=32 for these shots; more samples cost more time. The frozen sweep retained a million-stars allocation failure in both profiles. Mac reliability was not revalidated in that Linux run.

The water quickstart is a closed-shutter diagnostic. The full motion-blurred scene is much more expensive. It is a uniform-grid experiment with finite particle budgets, unresolved thin features and no two-way rigid-body coupling. It is not a general replacement for a mature simulation package. The VFX camera solve and single-view relief are estimates, with limitations documented beside the example.

Fog returns in 0.4 with a design independent of pause/resume. Broader simulation, reliability and performance on demanding scenes remain future directions, without promised release dates. Read vork help limits before committing to a shot.

Install

Upgrading scenes or scripts? Run vork help upgrade (upgrade guide).

Binary packages are available from GitHub Releases for Linux, Windows and Mac. Keep the entire install folder together: Slang, OIDN, libraries, examples, SDKs and licence texts are runtime companions to the binary.

  • Linux: x64, glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.30 (Ubuntu 22.04+), a recent NVIDIA GPU and its hardware-ray-tracing Vulkan driver.
  • Windows: x64 Windows 10/11, a recent NVIDIA GPU and its hardware-ray-tracing Vulkan driver.
  • Mac: Apple Silicon with Metal, macOS 26 for the bundled Slang toolchain. Older macOS versions are unqualified. Intel Macs are unsupported. H.264 uses system VideoToolbox.

For TypeScript authoring, install Node 22.18+ (with npm) from nodejs.org. For Python authoring, install Python 3.11+ from python.org or your platform's package manager. These runtimes are not bundled and are not needed for JSON scenes. Ubuntu 22.04's default Python 3.10 and Node packages are too old. On Ubuntu, install python3-venv for the distribution's Python, or the matching versioned venv package for your chosen Python (for example python3.12-venv). Use that Python 3.11+ executable in the commands below. Minimal Linux images also need xz-utils to unpack Node's .tar.xz download.

Linux

Install the NVIDIA driver for your GPU first. On Ubuntu 22.04+:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl tar libvulkan1 libgomp1 ffmpeg
curl -fL https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o /tmp/vork-install.sh
sh /tmp/vork-install.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
vork --version
vork help

These dependency commands are for Ubuntu with sudo. In a root container, omit sudo; without administrator access, arrange for the dependencies to be installed. The installer itself runs in your user account without root.

The installer verifies SHA256SUMS, installs under $HOME/.local/lib/vork, links $HOME/.local/bin/vork, runs vork setup, and adds the PATH line to your shell's startup files, including the one login shells read. The export above covers the current shell, and any shell that reads no startup file, such as plain bash -c. A custom PREFIX leaves startup files alone unless you also set VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1, which adds PREFIX/bin using the same shell startup files as the default install. For example: PREFIX="$HOME/tools/vork" VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh install.sh. VORK_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 always prevents PATH edits, including when opt-in is set. Linux MP4 needs ffmpeg even when NVENC encodes frames, because ffmpeg muxes the stream. Native NVENC is attempted on NVIDIA; otherwise encoding uses a readback fallback. Older GPUs and software Vulkan adapters are unsupported. A100, H100, H200, B200 and B300 lack the required hardware ray tracing; recency alone does not make an NVIDIA GPU suitable. Containers also need working NVIDIA Vulkan driver discovery; passing through a GPU alone may not be sufficient. If nvidia-smi works but Vulkan sees only llvmpipe, check the NVIDIA ICD JSON in /etc/vulkan/icd.d or /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d: its library may fail to load in a headless container. See Vulkan driver discovery.

Mac

The bundled Slang compiler requires macOS 26. Older macOS versions have not been qualified; a successful vork --version alone does not test Slang.

In Terminal:

curl -fL https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o /tmp/vork-install.sh
sh /tmp/vork-install.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
vork --version
vork help

The same installer verifies and installs the complete Apple Silicon archive under $HOME/.local/lib/vork, runs setup, and adds the PATH line to your shell's startup files (.zshenv for zsh). Mac packages are signed with Apple Developer ID and notarised.

MP4 uses VideoToolbox without ffmpeg. Install ffmpeg only for video decoding or encoding fallbacks, including MOV/ProRes fallback (brew install ffmpeg).

Windows

Install the NVIDIA driver for your GPU and ffmpeg (winget install Gyan.FFmpeg). Without winget (including Windows Server 2022), download ffmpeg-release-essentials.zip from Gyan, extract it, and add its bin folder to your user PATH. Open a new PowerShell window so ffmpeg is on PATH, then:

$installer = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'vork-install.ps1'
Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $installer
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $installer
$env:Path = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork;$env:Path"
vork --version
vork help

The installer itself runs in your user account without administrator rights.

The installer verifies SHA256SUMS, installs under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\vork, runs vork setup, and adds that folder to your user PATH so new windows find vork; the $env:Path line above covers the current one. A custom PREFIX leaves PATH alone unless $env:VORK_MODIFY_PATH='1' is also set; opt-in adds that folder to both the user PATH and the installer process's PATH. For example, set $env:PREFIX='D:\Tools\vork' and $env:VORK_MODIFY_PATH='1' before running the installer. VORK_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 always prevents PATH edits, including when opt-in is set. Windows MP4/MOV needs ffmpeg; MP4 uses its NVENC encoder when compatible, otherwise libx264. FFmpeg 9.0.2 requires NVENC API 13.1 (NVIDIA driver 610+) for hardware encoding; older drivers fall back to libx264. The cache is under %LOCALAPPDATA%\vork.

Manual archive install (Windows)

Download the Windows .zip and SHA256SUMS from the release page. Compare Get-FileHash .\vork-*-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 with its entry in SHA256SUMS, then unzip the entire contents into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\vork. Add that folder to your user PATH, open a new PowerShell window, and run vork setup. It prints the tools/GPU report and current phase; completion is marked by Shader setup completed. Time depends on the GPU, driver and cache. Keep all bundled runtime companions beside the executable.

Manual archive install (Linux or Mac)

The separately downloadable install.sh downloads the release from GitHub; to install an archive you already have without downloading again, use the manual steps below.

Download your platform's .tar.gz and SHA256SUMS from the release page into a new empty folder. In that folder, verify and install the entire archive:

set -- vork-*.tar.gz
test "$#" -eq 1 || exit 1
archive=$1
awk -v name="$archive" '$2 == name || $2 == "*" name' SHA256SUMS > selected.sha256
test "$(wc -l < selected.sha256 | tr -d ' ')" = 1 || exit 1
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sha256sum -c selected.sha256 || exit 1
else
  shasum -a 256 -c selected.sha256 || exit 1
fi
PREFIX="$HOME/.local"
mkdir tree
tar -xzf "$archive" -C tree
mkdir -p "$PREFIX/bin" "$PREFIX/lib/vork"
cp -R tree/. "$PREFIX/lib/vork/"
ln -sf "$PREFIX/lib/vork/vork" "$PREFIX/bin/vork"
export PATH="$PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
vork --version
vork setup

vork setup prints the tools/GPU report and current phase. Shader setup completed marks success; time depends on the GPU, driver and cache.

npm

Requires Node.js 22.18+ and a supported GPU and driver (above). Linux and Windows video output also needs ffmpeg.

npm create vork@latest my-shot
cd my-shot
npx vork setup
npx vork render scene.json --out render.png

This installs the engine and TypeScript SDK into the project; no global install is needed. In an existing project, npm install @voyager-so/vork and use npx vork the same way. Keep npm's optional dependencies enabled: they carry the platform runtime.

pip

Coming soon. Use the installers above for the Python SDK in the meantime.

First render and SDKs

Start with vork init my-shot and enter my-shot, then:

vork render scene.json --profile std/previs --out preview.png
vork render scene.json --profile std/final --out final.png
vork render scene.json --profile std/final --frame-start 0 --frame-end 23 --out clip.mp4
vork help animation
vork help outputs

The first render of a scene with new programs can compile for several minutes. Progress reports show shader and driver pipeline preparation; allow time for it to finish. Later renders reuse compiled programs and driver caches. Compilation time depends on the scene, GPU and cache state.

Frame ranges include both endpoints: 0 through 23 writes 24 frames. The simple scene is static; animation tracks make a moving clip. To try glTF import, save a model as model.glb beside this scene as model.json:

{"version":2,"nodes":[
  {"type":"asset","file":"model.glb"},
  {"type":"light","shape":"rectangle","translation":[-3,5,4],"target":[0,0,0],"energy":700,"size":4},
  {"type":"camera","translation":[3,2,5],"target":[0,0,0]}
],"render":{"resolution":[640,480]}}
vork render model.json --profile std/final --out model.png

Adjust the camera and light for your model's scale. glTF files can refer to textures and buffers beside them; keep those files together.

Setup warms the vork init starter at the default std/final profile on your GPU, with a ten-minute limit. Use vork setup --skip-warmup to check tools only; add --verbose for raw encoder probe diagnostics. You can interrupt setup safely: completed cache entries survive and remaining pipelines compile when needed. Run setup again to continue, or use vork setup --all for the exhaustive catalogue without the time limit. Device cache blobs are never included in the download.

Run vork setup again after upgrading or changing GPU drivers. It prints the tools/GPU report and current phase until Shader setup completed; time depends on the GPU, driver and cache. Vulkan persists its pipeline cache when supported; Metal warms the system driver cache. New scene programs can still require compilation on their first render. VORK_CACHE_DIR overrides the cache location.

The archive includes Python and TypeScript SDK source/packages, but not their runtimes. Install the Python SDK into your authoring virtual environment, and the TypeScript SDK into your project. TypeScript requires Node 22.18+ and npm. On older Node, upgrade (recommended), or run node --experimental-strip-types scene.ts instead of node scene.ts:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install "$HOME/.local/lib/vork/python"
npm install "$HOME/.local/lib/vork/sdk"

The SDKs install from your vork folder, not from npm or PyPI. The npm package named vork is unrelated, and the PyPI package only points back here.

On Windows (PowerShell):

py -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork\python"
npm install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork\sdk"

Use .venv\Scripts\python scene.py to run Python source on Windows. For a custom install, replace the default SDK paths above with your install folder. Import as vork in Python or @voyager-so/vork in TypeScript; keep the native executable on PATH. For source builds, see vork help build.

CPU rendering on Linux

Install recent Mesa Vulkan drivers (mesa-vulkan-drivers on Debian/Ubuntu; mesa-vulkan-drivers or vulkan-swrast elsewhere), then use vork setup --gpu cpu, then vork render scene.json --gpu cpu --out frame.png. Alternatively, set VORK_GPU=cpu for both commands. This requires ray queries and storage buffer arrays and is slow. CPU rendering is never chosen automatically. First-use compilation can take several minutes. vork's pipeline cache is disabled to avoid a lavapipe crash; portable shader artifacts and Mesa's own shader disk cache can still speed later runs. See build instructions for platform details.

Licence

See LICENSE for the terms. Third-party notices are in NOTICE. Assets and the stills in docs/images/ retain their own licences; keep the example credits with their renders. The optional Blender bridge has its own GPL licence and is not part of the renderer or SDK packages.

Give it to an agent Start with vork init, then vork help. Scene JSON uses the stable editor schema. Use vork help for the starting scene and concepts, vork help TOPIC --all for topic fields, and vork help field PATH for an exact field reference. Use the prompt above to start. Python and TypeScript can author ordinary scene JSON through the SDKs. You can also write JSON directly. For example, save this as scene.json (also available as examples/first-scene.json): {"version":2,"nodes":[ {"type":"mesh","geometry":{"std":"sphere","radius":1}, "materials":[{"inputs":{"base_color":[0.12,0.35,0.65],"specular_roughness":0.3}}]}, {"type":"mesh","translation":[0,-1,0],"geometry":{"std":"grid","size":[10,10]}, "materials":[{"inputs":{"base_color":[0.35,0.35,0.35]}}]}, {"type":"light","shape":"rectangle","translation":[-3,5,4],"target":[0,0,0], "energy":700,"size":4,"color":[1,0.92,0.8]}, {"type":"camera","translation":[3,2,5],"target":[0,0,0]} ],"render":{"resolution":[640,480]}} vork render scene.json --profile std/previs --out preview.png vork render scene.json --profile std/final --out final.png vork help sdk vork help programs --all Scene content and render quality are separate. Use std/previs to iterate, std/draft for scene-ray lighting at 4 samples, std/final for the default delivery profile, and std/path for path transport. Final approximates indirect lighting and can darken interiors, including glossy bounces. More samples do not restore omitted transport; try path and inspect. Draft and final use 4 and 8 samples with bundled OIDN denoising by default; use --set denoise=false to turn it off. --set samples=N overrides the profile budget (1..4096); more samples means cleaner and slower. Without a fast GPU denoiser (NVIDIA or Apple GPU), draft and final say so and use 16 and 32 samples undenoised; --set denoise=true runs the slow CPU denoiser anyway. For a particular field, ask vork help field node.target. Help topics include exact fields with --all. Images, video and control passes come from the same scene; see vork help outputs. Under the hood Default rendering combines raster visibility with hardware ray-traced lighting; a path tracer is also available. The scene and render plan stay installed. Frames use retained GPU resources, with GPU-to-hardware-video encoding on supported native paths. A portable encoding fallback reads pixels back to the CPU. Slang programs run on the GPU. Host parsing, planning, animation-track evaluation and IO still use the CPU. The public program hooks let a scene author change camera rays, material response, light propagation and film response without editing the renderer. vork help programs --all describes their scope. Validation includes furnace tests and analytic oracles, alongside render tests. That is a way to catch errors, not a guarantee that every scene is physically exact. Speed, with the qualifications These are timings, not equal-quality speedups. The draft/final results come from the build identified by SHA-256 in the results report on an NVIDIA L4: final uses eight samples and OIDN, draft four and OIDN. All 152 planned jobs were accounted for. The broader sweep delivered 583 of 585 images; the million-stars stress scene ran out of GPU memory in both profiles. Visual review found softer edges, grainier defocus, wall mottling and changed sparse or spectral highlights at these budgets. Nineteen earlier quality comparisons failed their declared no-worse FLIP condition; that experiment was not repeated for this build. vork times below are complete command wall times, including startup, scene loading, output writes and encoding. Research-preview limits Participating media (fog, haze, smoke and volumes) are unsupported in 0.3. Used medium bindings and volume topology are refused; removed programs such as std/fog fail lookup even in unused definitions. Bake an image plate and composite it, or render the medium externally. For a deliberately dry alternative, remove medium-only nodes, bindings and definitions while preserving shared surfaces. See vork help upgrade and vork help limits. Large scenes and dense transparency can fail, including on Mac; reducing image resolution alone does not necessarily fix them. Some heavy interiors work with std/path when the default hybrid profile fails. First use of a new program can involve substantial compilation, even after vork setup. At four/eight samples, fine facades and hair can lose detail, defocus can show stepped or grainy edges, and sparse sparks or spectral highlights can change brightness and colour. Try --set samples=32 for these shots; more samples cost more time. The frozen sweep retained a million-stars allocation failure in both profiles. Mac reliability was not revalidated in that Linux run. The water quickstart is a closed-shutter diagnostic. The full motion-blurred scene is much more expensive. It is a uniform-grid experiment with finite particle budgets, unresolved thin features and no two-way rigid-body coupling. It is not a general replacement for a mature simulation package. The VFX camera solve and single-view relief are estimates, with limitations documented beside the example. Fog returns in 0.4 with a design independent of pause/resume. Broader simulation, reliability and performance on demanding scenes remain future directions, without promised release dates. Read vork help limits before committing to a shot. Install Upgrading scenes or scripts? Run vork help upgrade (upgrade guide). Binary packages are available from GitHub Releases for Linux, Windows and Mac. Keep the entire install folder together: Slang, OIDN, libraries, examples, SDKs and licence texts are runtime companions to the binary. Linux: x64, glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.30 (Ubuntu 22.04+), a recent NVIDIA GPU and its hardware-ray-tracing Vulkan driver. Windows: x64 Windows 10/11, a recent NVIDIA GPU and its hardware-ray-tracing Vulkan driver. Mac: Apple Silicon with Metal, macOS 26 for the bundled Slang toolchain. Older macOS versions are unqualified. Intel Macs are unsupported. H.264 uses system VideoToolbox. For TypeScript authoring, install Node 22.18+ (with npm) from nodejs.org. For Python authoring, install Python 3.11+ from python.org or your platform's package manager. These runtimes are not bundled and are not needed for JSON scenes. Ubuntu 22.04's default Python 3.10 and Node packages are too old. On Ubuntu, install python3-venv for the distribution's Python, or the matching versioned venv package for your chosen Python (for example python3.12-venv). Use that Python 3.11+ executable in the commands below. Minimal Linux images also need xz-utils to unpack Node's .tar.xz download. Linux Install the NVIDIA driver for your GPU first. On Ubuntu 22.04+: sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl tar libvulkan1 libgomp1 ffmpeg curl -fL https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o /tmp/vork-install.sh sh /tmp/vork-install.sh export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" vork --version vork help These dependency commands are for Ubuntu with sudo. In a root container, omit sudo; without administrator access, arrange for the dependencies to be installed. The installer itself runs in your user account without root. The installer verifies SHA256SUMS, installs under $HOME/.local/lib/vork, links $HOME/.local/bin/vork, runs vork setup, and adds the PATH line to your shell's startup files, including the one login shells read. The export above covers the current shell, and any shell that reads no startup file, such as plain bash -c. A custom PREFIX leaves startup files alone unless you also set VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1, which adds PREFIX/bin using the same shell startup files as the default install. For example: PREFIX="$HOME/tools/vork" VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh install.sh. VORK_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 always prevents PATH edits, including when opt-in is set. Linux MP4 needs ffmpeg even when NVENC encodes frames, because ffmpeg muxes the stream. Native NVENC is attempted on NVIDIA; otherwise encoding uses a readback fallback. Older GPUs and software Vulkan adapters are unsupported. A100, H100, H200, B200 and B300 lack the required hardware ray tracing; recency alone does not make an NVIDIA GPU suitable. Containers also need working NVIDIA Vulkan driver discovery; passing through a GPU alone may not be sufficient. If nvidia-smi works but Vulkan sees only llvmpipe, check the NVIDIA ICD JSON in /etc/vulkan/icd.d or /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d: its library may fail to load in a headless container. See Vulkan driver discovery. Mac The bundled Slang compiler requires macOS 26. Older macOS versions have not been qualified; a successful vork --version alone does not test Slang. In Terminal: curl -fL https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o /tmp/vork-install.sh sh /tmp/vork-install.sh export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" vork --version vork help The same installer verifies and installs the complete Apple Silicon archive under $HOME/.local/lib/vork, runs setup, and adds the PATH line to your shell's startup files (.zshenv for zsh). Mac packages are signed with Apple Developer ID and notarised. MP4 uses VideoToolbox without ffmpeg. Install ffmpeg only for video decoding or encoding fallbacks, including MOV/ProRes fallback (brew install ffmpeg). Windows Install the NVIDIA driver for your GPU and ffmpeg (winget install Gyan.FFmpeg). Without winget (including Windows Server 2022), download ffmpeg-release-essentials.zip from Gyan, extract it, and add its bin folder to your user PATH. Open a new PowerShell window so ffmpeg is on PATH, then: $installer = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'vork-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $installer powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $installer $env:Path = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork;$env:Path" vork --version vork help The installer itself runs in your user account without administrator rights. The installer verifies SHA256SUMS, installs under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\vork, runs vork setup, and adds that folder to your user PATH so new windows find vork; the $env:Path line above covers the current one. A custom PREFIX leaves PATH alone unless $env:VORK_MODIFY_PATH='1' is also set; opt-in adds that folder to both the user PATH and the installer process's PATH. For example, set $env:PREFIX='D:\Tools\vork' and $env:VORK_MODIFY_PATH='1' before running the installer. VORK_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 always prevents PATH edits, including when opt-in is set. Windows MP4/MOV needs ffmpeg; MP4 uses its NVENC encoder when compatible, otherwise libx264. FFmpeg 9.0.2 requires NVENC API 13.1 (NVIDIA driver 610+) for hardware encoding; older drivers fall back to libx264. The cache is under %LOCALAPPDATA%\vork. Manual archive install (Windows) Download the Windows .zip and SHA256SUMS from the release page. Compare Get-FileHash .\vork-*-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 with its entry in SHA256SUMS, then unzip the entire contents into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\vork. Add that folder to your user PATH, open a new PowerShell window, and run vork setup. It prints the tools/GPU report and current phase; completion is marked by Shader setup completed. Time depends on the GPU, driver and cache. Keep all bundled runtime companions beside the executable. Manual archive install (Linux or Mac) The separately downloadable install.sh downloads the release from GitHub; to install an archive you already have without downloading again, use the manual steps below. Download your platform's .tar.gz and SHA256SUMS from the release page into a new empty folder. In that folder, verify and install the entire archive: set -- vork-*.tar.gz test "$#" -eq 1 || exit 1 archive=$1 awk -v name="$archive" '$2 == name || $2 == "*" name' SHA256SUMS > selected.sha256 test "$(wc -l < selected.sha256 | tr -d ' ')" = 1 || exit 1 if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum -c selected.sha256 || exit 1 else shasum -a 256 -c selected.sha256 || exit 1 fi PREFIX="$HOME/.local" mkdir tree tar -xzf "$archive" -C tree mkdir -p "$PREFIX/bin" "$PREFIX/lib/vork" cp -R tree/. "$PREFIX/lib/vork/" ln -sf "$PREFIX/lib/vork/vork" "$PREFIX/bin/vork" export PATH="$PREFIX/bin:$PATH" vork --version vork setup vork setup prints the tools/GPU report and current phase. Shader setup completed marks success; time depends on the GPU, driver and cache. npm Requires Node.js 22.18+ and a supported GPU and driver (above). Linux and Windows video output also needs ffmpeg. npm create vork@latest my-shot cd my-shot npx vork setup npx vork render scene.json --out render.png This installs the engine and TypeScript SDK into the project; no global install is needed. In an existing project, npm install @voyager-so/vork and use npx vork the same way. Keep npm's optional dependencies enabled: they carry the platform runtime. pip Coming soon. Use the installers above for the Python SDK in the meantime. First render and SDKs Start with vork init my-shot and enter my-shot, then: vork render scene.json --profile std/previs --out preview.png vork render scene.json --profile std/final --out final.png vork render scene.json --profile std/final --frame-start 0 --frame-end 23 --out clip.mp4 vork help animation vork help outputs The first render of a scene with new programs can compile for several minutes. Progress reports show shader and driver pipeline preparation; allow time for it to finish. Later renders reuse compiled programs and driver caches. Compilation time depends on the scene, GPU and cache state. Frame ranges include both endpoints: 0 through 23 writes 24 frames. The simple scene is static; animation tracks make a moving clip. To try glTF import, save a model as model.glb beside this scene as model.json: {"version":2,"nodes":[ {"type":"asset","file":"model.glb"}, {"type":"light","shape":"rectangle","translation":[-3,5,4],"target":[0,0,0],"energy":700,"size":4}, {"type":"camera","translation":[3,2,5],"target":[0,0,0]} ],"render":{"resolution":[640,480]}} vork render model.json --profile std/final --out model.png Adjust the camera and light for your model's scale. glTF files can refer to textures and buffers beside them; keep those files together. Setup warms the vork init starter at the default std/final profile on your GPU, with a ten-minute limit. Use vork setup --skip-warmup to check tools only; add --verbose for raw encoder probe diagnostics. You can interrupt setup safely: completed cache entries survive and remaining pipelines compile when needed. Run setup again to continue, or use vork setup --all for the exhaustive catalogue without the time limit. Device cache blobs are never included in the download. Run vork setup again after upgrading or changing GPU drivers. It prints the tools/GPU report and current phase until Shader setup completed; time depends on the GPU, driver and cache. Vulkan persists its pipeline cache when supported; Metal warms the system driver cache. New scene programs can still require compilation on their first render. VORK_CACHE_DIR overrides the cache location. The archive includes Python and TypeScript SDK source/packages, but not their runtimes. Install the Python SDK into your authoring virtual environment, and the TypeScript SDK into your project. TypeScript requires Node 22.18+ and npm. On older Node, upgrade (recommended), or run node --experimental-strip-types scene.ts instead of node scene.ts: python3 -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install "$HOME/.local/lib/vork/python" npm install "$HOME/.local/lib/vork/sdk" The SDKs install from your vork folder, not from npm or PyPI. The npm package named vork is unrelated, and the PyPI package only points back here. On Windows (PowerShell): py -m venv .venv .venv\Scripts\python -m pip install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork\python" npm install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork\sdk" Use .venv\Scripts\python scene.py to run Python source on Windows. For a custom install, replace the default SDK paths above with your install folder. Import as vork in Python or @voyager-so/vork in TypeScript; keep the native executable on PATH. For source builds, see vork help build. CPU rendering on Linux Install recent Mesa Vulkan drivers (mesa-vulkan-drivers on Debian/Ubuntu; mesa-vulkan-drivers or vulkan-swrast elsewhere), then use vork setup --gpu cpu, then vork render scene.json --gpu cpu --out frame.png. Alternatively, set VORK_GPU=cpu for both commands. This requires ray queries and storage buffer arrays and is slow. CPU rendering is never chosen automatically. First-use compilation can take several minutes. vork's pipeline cache is disabled to avoid a lavapipe crash; portable shader artifacts and Mesa's own shader disk cache can still speed later runs. See build instructions for platform details. Licence See LICENSE for the terms. Third-party notices are in NOTICE. Assets and the stills in docs/images/ retain their own licences; keep the example credits with their renders. The optional Blender bridge has its own GPL licence and is not part of the renderer or SDK packages.

blocks.html_en: Scene content and render quality are separate. Use std/previs to iterate, std/draft for scene-ray lighting at 4 samples, std/final for the default delivery profile, and std/path for path transport. Final approximates indirect lighting and can darken interiors, including glossy bounces. More samples do not restore omitted transport; try path and inspect. Draft and final use 4 and 8 samples with bundled OIDN denoising by default; use --set denoise=false to turn it off. --set samples=N overrides the profile budget (1..4096); more samples means cleaner and slower. Without a fast GPU denoiser (NVIDIA or Apple GPU), draft and final say so and use 16 and 32 samples undenoised; --set denoise=true runs the slow CPU denoiser anyway. For a particular field, ask vork help field node.target. Help topics include exact fields with --all. Images, video and control passes come from the same scene; see vork help outputs.

blocks.html_en: The installer verifies SHA256SUMS, installs under $HOME/.local/lib/vork, links $HOME/.local/bin/vork, runs vork setup, and adds the PATH line to your shell's startup files, including the one login shells read. The export above covers the current shell, and any shell that reads no startup file, such as plain bash -c. A custom PREFIX leaves startup files alone unless you also set VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1, which adds PREFIX/bin using the same shell startup files as the default install. For example: PREFIX="$HOME/tools/vork" VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh install.sh. VORK_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 always prevents PATH edits, including when opt-in is set. Linux MP4 needs ffmpeg even when NVENC encodes frames, because ffmpeg muxes the stream. Native NVENC is attempted on NVIDIA; otherwise encoding uses a readback fallback. content_html_zh:
vork is a 3D and VFX engine built for AI agents.

Agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens.

skim-hero.mp4

One million birds, each on its own path. 192 frames at 1080p rendered in 97 seconds on a single NVIDIA L4. Blender EEVEE at the same sample count is projected at 13–18 minutes. How we measured · how it's made · credits

  • Built for agents: a small API that agents can extend with their own GPU programs.
  • Fast: 1.1–2.3× faster than EEVEE on default stills and movies, and about 8–11× on the bird flock. Speed, with the qualifications.
  • Native GPU engine: written in Rust and Slang, runs on Vulkan and Metal (Linux, Windows, macOS).

Paste this to your agent

Install vork, then paste:

Run vork init my-shot, read vork help, render a preview and inspect the image. Refine the camera and lighting before rendering at final quality. Read the relevant help topic when you need a feature the first page doesn't explain.

vork is written in Rust and Slang, with GPU rendering through Vulkan and Metal. An agent writes a scene, renders it, looks at the result and revises the code. There is no editor to drive.

Most creative tools expose controls that a person can operate. An agent can also write a shader in the middle of a shot. vork gives it geometry, ray queries and GPU execution, then lets scene programs define materials, cameras, light propagation, simulation and compositing. Ordinary shots need only scene data; the programming hooks are there when the shot needs something unusual.

Source-available and free during the research preview.

从这里开始

After installing vork, create a working project:

vork init my-shot
cd my-shot
vork render scene.json --out render.png
vork help

Open render.png, change a colour or camera position in scene.json, and render again. The starter uses only bundled sphere, box and grid primitives: no downloads, no GPU needed to initialize. Use vork init my-shot --language typescript or --language python for editable scene.ts or scene.py alongside the ready-to-render JSON. The generated README explains regeneration and SDK requirements. Existing files are never overwritten. The default std/final profile is warmed by setup; use --profile std/draft for quicker previews.

What you can make

The examples include code, preparation commands and credits. Large downloaded assets and footage stay outside Git; the recipes fetch them or accept a local path. The images here are stills from these shots. Keep each credit with its image.

Million birds

A million simulated agents steered by Slang compute programs, with a camera skimming through the flock. The camera and nine foreground birds are authored; the simulated million do not flap. The bird stills above come from the measured four-sample, denoised skim and reveal movies.

Credit: based on "Crow" by Alexei Ostapenko, CC BY 4.0. Changes: sampled flight pose, reduced distant mesh, rescaled, articulated flight wings, extracted wings for the starling body, resized textures. All bird and environment credits.

Cyber car

Watch the film: a car drives into the night as the forest turns into glowing cyan wireframe, drawn from real triangle edges by a scene shader.

Credit: “Car Concept” by Unity Fan, glTF adaptation by Eric Chadwick / Darmstadt Graphics Group, CC BY 4.0. Changes: scaled, animated, brighter head and tail lights, wheel pose. Trees, ground and asphalt from Poly Haven (CC0). The far mountains and sky are an image-model painting on a curved 3D card; everything else that moves is rendered.

VFX on real footage

Original footage Tracked camera and proxy geometry Final look

A procedural ceramic-and-bronze seed, a tracked camera, occlusion mattes and proxy geometry for relighting. The example teaches the base composite; the final look adds later relighting and wipes. Real footage + rendered 3D; no generative video.

Credit: footage by Ron Lach / Pexels, modified under the Pexels Licence. Original performer; no endorsement implied. Source and preparation.

After Rain

A suspended neon seed and blade sign added to a moving shot of an empty alley at night, with spill on the wall and reflections in the wet street. Real footage + rendered 3D; no generative video.

Credit: footage is "Ally" by Rafael Fernanz / Pexels, modified under the Pexels Licence. Source and preparation.

Black hole

The scene supplies a Schwarzschild light-propagation program through vork's public hook. Curved paths, capture and the disk's appearance live in the example. It is a numerical approximation, not an exact relativistic solver.

Credit: based on "Corinth Cargo Transporter" by Yvo Pors, CC BY 4.0. Changes: decimated geometry, resized, compressed and exposure-adjusted textures, adjusted material roughness and metallic weight, placement and scale. Ship credit.

Cake

A moving camera, depth of field and daylight on detailed scanned assets. This shot is rendered 3D, using Poly Haven assets; it isn't a photographed take.

Credit: Poly Haven CC0 assets; carrot cake photography by Greg Zaal, processing by James Ray Cock. Full cake credits.

Cozy Kitchen

Nicole Morena's Blender 3.5 splash scene, imported into vork. The recipe uses a shared material adaptation and a camera orbit; the pictured render has additional staging and animated lighting.

Credit: Cozy Kitchen by Nicole Morena, source .blend, CC BY-SA (version unspecified by source). Adapted and rendered in vork: camera orbit, animated lighting, widescreen framing, material translation and staging changes. This still and the adapted animation are shared under CC BY-SA. No artist endorsement implied. Changes and share-alike notice.

Water

A GPU liquid simulation implemented as Slang compute programs in vork's fluid library. It uses published APIC/FLIP and surface-reconstruction methods, with an authored initial impulse and limited secondary spray.

No suitable GPU?

Rendering requires Apple Silicon or an NVIDIA GPU with Vulkan ray queries. Scene authoring and vork help work without a GPU. On your own NVIDIA Linux machine, you can use the Docker runtime.

Give it to an agent

Start with vork init, then vork help. Scene JSON uses the stable editor schema. Use vork help for the starting scene and concepts, vork help TOPIC --all for topic fields, and vork help field PATH for an exact field reference.

Use the prompt above to start.

Python and TypeScript can author ordinary scene JSON through the SDKs. You can also write JSON directly. For example, save this as scene.json (also available as examples/first-scene.json):

{"version":2,"nodes":[
  {"type":"mesh","geometry":{"std":"sphere","radius":1},
   "materials":[{"inputs":{"base_color":[0.12,0.35,0.65],"specular_roughness":0.3}}]},
  {"type":"mesh","translation":[0,-1,0],"geometry":{"std":"grid","size":[10,10]},
   "materials":[{"inputs":{"base_color":[0.35,0.35,0.35]}}]},
  {"type":"light","shape":"rectangle","translation":[-3,5,4],"target":[0,0,0],
   "energy":700,"size":4,"color":[1,0.92,0.8]},
  {"type":"camera","translation":[3,2,5],"target":[0,0,0]}
],"render":{"resolution":[640,480]}}
vork render scene.json --profile std/previs --out preview.png
vork render scene.json --profile std/final --out final.png
vork help sdk
vork help programs --all

Scene content and render quality are separate. Use std/previs to iterate, std/draft for scene-ray lighting at 4 samples, std/final for the default delivery profile, and std/path for path transport. Final approximates indirect lighting and can darken interiors, including glossy bounces. More samples do not restore omitted transport; try path and inspect. Draft and final use 4 and 8 samples with bundled OIDN denoising by default; use --set denoise=false to turn it off. --set samples=N overrides the profile budget (1..4096); more samples means cleaner and slower. Without a fast GPU denoiser (NVIDIA or Apple GPU), draft and final say so and use 16 and 32 samples undenoised; --set denoise=true runs the slow CPU denoiser anyway. For a particular field, ask vork help field node.target. Help topics include exact fields with --all. Images, video and control passes come from the same scene; see vork help outputs.

在引擎盖下

Default rendering combines raster visibility with hardware ray-traced lighting; a path tracer is also available. The scene and render plan stay installed. Frames use retained GPU resources, with GPU-to-hardware-video encoding on supported native paths. A portable encoding fallback reads pixels back to the CPU.

Slang programs run on the GPU. Host parsing, planning, animation-track evaluation and IO still use the CPU. The public program hooks let a scene author change camera rays, material response, light propagation and film response without editing the renderer. vork help programs --all describes their scope.

Validation includes furnace tests and analytic oracles, alongside render tests. That is a way to catch errors, not a guarantee that every scene is physically exact.

Speed, with the qualifications

These are timings, not equal-quality speedups. The draft/final results come from the build identified by SHA-256 in the results report on an NVIDIA L4: final uses eight samples and OIDN, draft four and OIDN. All 152 planned jobs were accounted for. The broader sweep delivered 583 of 585 images; the million-stars stress scene ran out of GPU memory in both profiles. Visual review found softer edges, grainier defocus, wall mottling and changed sparse or spectral highlights at these budgets. Nineteen earlier quality comparisons failed their declared no-worse FLIP condition; that experiment was not repeated for this build.

vork times below are complete command wall times, including startup, scene loading, output writes and encoding. Setup, shader warmup, provisioning and transfers are excluded. Stills use five warm repetitions, movies three. Driver caches and clocks were not controlled. Blender 5.2.1 times are retained measured baselines, not fresh runs: EEVEE uses different settings, and its movie times exclude startup/loading after a still prime. Both movie timings include encoding. The car is a proxy. Benchmark method and recorded results explain the boundaries and carried-forward numbers.

Research-preview limits

Participating media (fog, haze, smoke and volumes) are unsupported in 0.3. Used medium bindings and volume topology are refused; removed programs such as std/fog fail lookup even in unused definitions. Bake an image plate and composite it, or render the medium externally. For a deliberately dry alternative, remove medium-only nodes, bindings and definitions while preserving shared surfaces. See vork help upgrade and vork help limits.

Large scenes and dense transparency can fail, including on Mac; reducing image resolution alone does not necessarily fix them. Some heavy interiors work with std/path when the default hybrid profile fails. First use of a new program can involve substantial compilation, even after vork setup.

At four/eight samples, fine facades and hair can lose detail, defocus can show stepped or grainy edges, and sparse sparks or spectral highlights can change brightness and colour. Try --set samples=32 for these shots; more samples cost more time. The frozen sweep retained a million-stars allocation failure in both profiles. Mac reliability was not revalidated in that Linux run.

The water quickstart is a closed-shutter diagnostic. The full motion-blurred scene is much more expensive. It is a uniform-grid experiment with finite particle budgets, unresolved thin features and no two-way rigid-body coupling. It is not a general replacement for a mature simulation package. The VFX camera solve and single-view relief are estimates, with limitations documented beside the example.

Fog returns in 0.4 with a design independent of pause/resume. Broader simulation, reliability and performance on demanding scenes remain future directions, without promised release dates. Read vork help limits before committing to a shot.

安装

Upgrading scenes or scripts? Run vork help upgrade (upgrade guide).

Binary packages are available from GitHub Releases for Linux, Windows and Mac. Keep the entire install folder together: Slang, OIDN, libraries, examples, SDKs and licence texts are runtime companions to the binary.

  • Linux: x64, glibc 2.35+ and libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.30 (Ubuntu 22.04+), a recent NVIDIA GPU and its hardware-ray-tracing Vulkan driver.
  • Windows: x64 Windows 10/11, a recent NVIDIA GPU and its hardware-ray-tracing Vulkan driver.
  • Mac: Apple Silicon with Metal, macOS 26 for the bundled Slang toolchain. Older macOS versions are unqualified. Intel Macs are unsupported. H.264 uses system VideoToolbox.

For TypeScript authoring, install Node 22.18+ (with npm) from nodejs.org. For Python authoring, install Python 3.11+ from python.org or your platform's package manager. These runtimes are not bundled and are not needed for JSON scenes. Ubuntu 22.04's default Python 3.10 and Node packages are too old. On Ubuntu, install python3-venv for the distribution's Python, or the matching versioned venv package for your chosen Python (for example python3.12-venv). Use that Python 3.11+ executable in the commands below. Minimal Linux images also need xz-utils to unpack Node's .tar.xz download.

Linux

Install the NVIDIA driver for your GPU first. On Ubuntu 22.04+:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl tar libvulkan1 libgomp1 ffmpeg
curl -fL https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o /tmp/vork-install.sh
sh /tmp/vork-install.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
vork --version
vork help

These dependency commands are for Ubuntu with sudo. In a root container, omit sudo; without administrator access, arrange for the dependencies to be installed. The installer itself runs in your user account without root.

The installer verifies SHA256SUMS, installs under $HOME/.local/lib/vork, links $HOME/.local/bin/vork, runs vork setup, and adds the PATH line to your shell's startup files, including the one login shells read. The export above covers the current shell, and any shell that reads no startup file, such as plain bash -c. A custom PREFIX leaves startup files alone unless you also set VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1, which adds PREFIX/bin using the same shell startup files as the default install. For example: PREFIX="$HOME/tools/vork" VORK_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh install.sh. VORK_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 always prevents PATH edits, including when opt-in is set. Linux MP4 needs ffmpeg even when NVENC encodes frames, because ffmpeg muxes the stream. Native NVENC is attempted on NVIDIA; otherwise encoding uses a readback fallback. Older GPUs and software Vulkan adapters are unsupported. A100, H100, H200, B200 and B300 lack the required hardware ray tracing; recency alone does not make an NVIDIA GPU suitable. Containers also need working NVIDIA Vulkan driver discovery; passing through a GPU alone may not be sufficient. If nvidia-smi works but Vulkan sees only llvmpipe, check the NVIDIA ICD JSON in /etc/vulkan/icd.d or /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d: its library may fail to load in a headless container. See Vulkan driver discovery.

In Terminal:

curl -fL https://github.com/voyager-so/vork/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o /tmp/vork-install.sh
sh /tmp/vork-install.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

The installer verifies SHA256SUMS, installs under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\vork, runs vork setup, and adds that folder to your user PATH so new windows find vork; the $env:Path line above covers the current one. Manual archive install (Windows)

Download the Windows .zip and SHA256SUMS from the release page. Compare Get-FileHash .\vork-*-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 with its entry in SHA256SUMS, then unzip the entire contents into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\vork. Add that folder to your user PATH, open a new PowerShell window, and run vork setup. It prints the tools/GPU report and current phase; completion is marked by Shader setup completed. Time depends on the GPU, driver and cache. Keep all bundled runtime companions beside the executable.

Manual archive install (Linux or Mac)

The separately downloadable install.sh downloads the release from GitHub; to install an archive you already have without downloading again, use the manual steps below.

Download your platform's .tar.gz and SHA256SUMS from the release page into a new empty folder. In that folder, verify and install the entire archive:

set -- vork-*.tar.gz
test "$#" -eq 1 || exit 1
archive=$1
awk -v name="$archive" '$2 == name || $2 == "*" name' SHA256SUMS > selected.sha256
test "$(wc -l < selected.sha256 | tr -d ' ')" = 1 || exit 1
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sha256sum -c selected.sha256 || exit 1
else
  shasum -a 256 -c selected.sha256 || exit 1
fi
PREFIX="$HOME/.local"
mkdir tree
tar -xzf "$archive" -C tree
mkdir -p "$PREFIX/bin" "$PREFIX/lib/vork"
cp -R tree/. "$PREFIX/lib/vork/"
ln -sf "$PREFIX/lib/vork/vork" "$PREFIX/bin/vork"
export PATH="$PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
vork --version
vork setup

vork setup prints the tools/GPU report and current phase. Shader setup completed marks success; time depends on the GPU, driver and cache.

First render and SDKs

Start with vork init my-shot and enter my-shot, then:

vork render scene.json --profile std/previs --out preview.png
vork render scene.json --profile std/final --out final.png
vork render scene.json --profile std/final --frame-start 0 --frame-end 23 --out clip.mp4
vork help animation
vork help outputs

The first render of a scene with new programs can compile for several minutes. Progress reports show shader and driver pipeline preparation; allow time for it to finish. Later renders reuse compiled programs and driver caches. Compilation time depends on the scene, GPU and cache state.

Frame ranges include both endpoints: 0 through 23 writes 24 frames. The simple scene is static; animation tracks make a moving clip. To try glTF import, save a model as model.glb beside this scene as model.json:

{"version":2,"nodes":[
  {"type":"asset","file":"model.glb"},
  {"type":"light","shape":"rectangle","translation":[-3,5,4],"target":[0,0,0],"energy":700,"size":4},
  {"type":"camera","translation":[3,2,5],"target":[0,0,0]}
],"render":{"resolution":[640,480]}}
vork render model.json --profile std/final --out model.png

Adjust the camera and light for your model's scale. glTF files can refer to textures and buffers beside them; keep those files together.

Setup warms the vork init starter at the default std/final profile on your GPU, with a ten-minute limit. Use vork setup --skip-warmup to check tools only; add --verbose for raw encoder probe diagnostics. You can interrupt setup safely: completed cache entries survive and remaining pipelines compile when needed. Run setup again to continue, or use vork setup --all for the exhaustive catalogue without the time limit. Device cache blobs are never included in the download.

Run vork setup again after upgrading or changing GPU drivers. It prints the tools/GPU report and current phase until Shader setup completed; time depends on the GPU, driver and cache. Vulkan persists its pipeline cache when supported; Metal warms the system driver cache. New scene programs can still require compilation on their first render. VORK_CACHE_DIR overrides the cache location.

The archive includes Python and TypeScript SDK source/packages, but not their runtimes. Install the Python SDK into your authoring virtual environment, and the TypeScript SDK into your project. TypeScript requires Node 22.18+ and npm. On older Node, upgrade (recommended), or run node --experimental-strip-types scene.ts instead of node scene.ts:

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install "$HOME/.local/lib/vork/python"
npm install "$HOME/.local/lib/vork/sdk"

The SDKs install from your vork folder, not from npm or PyPI. The npm package named vork is unrelated, and the PyPI package only points back here.

On Windows (PowerShell):

py -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork\python"
npm install "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\vork\sdk"

Use .venv\Scripts\python scene.py to run Python source on Windows. For a custom install, replace the default SDK paths above with your install folder. Import as vork in Python or @voyager-so/vork in TypeScript; keep the native executable on PATH. For source builds, see vork help build.

CPU rendering on Linux

Install recent Mesa Vulkan drivers (mesa-vulkan-drivers on Debian/Ubuntu; mesa-vulkan-drivers or vulkan-swrast elsewhere), then use vork setup --gpu cpu, then vork render scene.json --gpu cpu --out frame.png. Alternatively, set VORK_GPU=cpu for both commands. This requires ray queries and storage buffer arrays and is slow. CPU rendering is never chosen automatically. First-use compilation can take several minutes. vork's pipeline cache is disabled to avoid a lavapipe crash; portable shader artifacts and Mesa's own shader disk cache can still speed later runs. See build instructions for platform details.
